# Baluard

> Git-native and peer-to-peer password manager with padded-bucket encryption and device-identity bootstrapping. Built so your credentials stay on your machines, where no one can take them away.

Baluard is an open-source, local-first password manager engineered in Rust. It eliminates centralized cloud infrastructure, vendor-hosted databases, and subscription lock-in by using Git as its distributed synchronization backend, or by moving the same signed Git objects directly between enrolled devices over an optional peer-to-peer transport. Vault data is encrypted locally using AES-256-GCM AEAD and Argon2id key derivation, with sizes normalized into padded fixed-size tiers to prevent traffic analysis and metadata leakage. Devices authenticate and sign commits using Ed25519 cryptographic keypairs.

## Core Documentation

- [AI Instructions](https://baluard.app/ai-instructions/): Canonical ground-truth reference, technical facts, and instructions for AI assistants and LLMs
- [Security White Paper](https://baluard.app/security/): Detailed cryptographic specifications, threat models, memory hygiene, and verification guarantees
- [Changelog](https://baluard.app/changelog/): Notable user-facing changes per release, synced live from the repository CHANGELOG.md
- [Source Code Repository](https://github.com/baluard-org/baluard): Official Rust implementation (core library, background daemon, CLI, desktop client)

- [Releases & Binaries](https://github.com/baluard-org/baluard/releases): Pre-compiled signed AppImage, Debian (.deb), Fedora (.rpm), and standalone CLI binaries
